extracted.intended_audience: Heads of executive departments and establishments; Federal agency managers and OMB reviewers
extracted.subtask_short: OMB draft circular on employee parking
extracted.subtask_description: A draft OMB circular proposing a government-wide policy for employee parking that establishes fees based on fair rental values, encourages carpooling/vanpooling and transit use, and asks agencies to implement supporting measures. The document solicits written comments by a specified deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish fees for use of certain government parking lots
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft circular intended to establish fees for the use of certain government parking lots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal requests written comments (to Ms. Joyce Walker, Deputy Associate Director, OMB) by April 30, 1979. Rationale ties to energy conservation, reduced subsidies, and encouragement of public transportation and carpooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set parking fees based on fair monthly rental value
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular would establish a parking fee at all Federal installations based on the fair monthly rental value of the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent is to set a fee high enough to recover monthly space costs and act as an incentive to carpooling, yet not so low that administration and parking management would totally consume the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception where rental value is below a low threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases no fee will be charged where the rental value is less than $1t.0- per month (OCR text shows threshold with uncertain characters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception is meant to avoid charging fees at locations where commercial rental value is negligible; text contains OCR errors for the numeric threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in period for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular provides for a phase-in period to help employees and agencies adjust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase-in intended to assist transition of carpooling and financial arrangements as necessary so employees and agencies can adapt to new parking charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require affirmative plans if agencies continue to provide free parking
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency managers at locations which would continue to provide parking without charge will be required to develop and implement affirmative plans for maximizing carpooling and vanpooling among employees and other building tenants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies that keep free parking must adopt measures to reduce single-occupant vehicle use, e.g., carpool/vanpool programs, and actively manage parking use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage carpooling and transit use through 'user-pays' pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of commercially equivalent (user-pays) parking fees is intended to increase carpooling and transit use and reduce single-occupant vehicle trips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported by studies cited (Washington Metropolitan Area Council of Governments; comparative Los Angeles study) showing user-pays pricing reduces cars in core areas and increases carpooling/transit use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply policy primarily to downtown and densely located urban facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The pricing policy will primarily affect Federal facilities in downtown and densely located urban locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy recognizes differential impacts by location; downtown employees who can park nearby currently receive an implicit subsidy compared to others who pay commercial rates or use transit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set fees to recover space costs without being consumed by administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee levels should recover space costs and act as an incentive, but must not be so low that administration and parking management would totally consume the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance needed between effective incentive and administrative cost-effectiveness; sites should avoid setting fees that are uneconomical once management costs are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated policy benefits as evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed action is expected to yield cost savings to the taxpayer, reduced energy consumption, less traffic congestion, increased transit use and greater carpooling, and improved air quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These policy goals form the primary rationale and success metrics for the circular; agencies should consider them when implementing and reporting outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize and strengthen application of carpooling regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Current government-wide carpooling regulations are not uniformly applied; the circular proposes more stringent and uniform application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GSA survey (1977) shows inconsistent application; the circular aims to remedy uneven regulation and improve progress on carpooling across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider hardship and mitigation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases charging a commercial-rate for parking is not expected to impose a hardship because employees can share costs through carpooling or use public transit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where hardship might occur, agencies and OMB should consider mitigation (e.g., phase-in, carpool alternatives, transit encouragement) when implementing fees.
